questions.question: In an $m\times n$ matrix, what do $m$ and $n$ count?
options: $m$ counts diagonal entries and $n$ counts nonzero entries.

questions.question: What kind of object is a matrix?
options: A single scalar with a chosen name.
A rectangular array of field elements in rows and columns
A set containing only vectors of length one.
A rule that must always map vectors to vectors.

questions.question: Why is the order “rows then columns” important when giving the size of a matrix?
options: Because a $2\times3$ matrix and a $3\times2$ matrix have different shapes.
Because rows and columns are interchangeable in matrix size notation.
Because every matrix has the same number of rows and columns.
Because the number of columns is never written.

questions.question: What is one reason matrices appear in linear algebra?
options: They replace the need for fields.
They turn every vector space into the real line.
They store coefficients and represent maps in coordinates
They make every system of equations inconsistent.

questions.question: How can a matrix be viewed in terms of vectors?
options: As a set with no order among its entries.
Only as a polynomial in one variable.
As a list of column vectors or row vectors

questions.question: What is the size of $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\4&5&6\end{pmatrix}$?
How many entries does a $4\times5$ matrix have?
Which matrix has size $3\times1$?
In the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}7&8\\9&10\\11&12\end{pmatrix}$, what is the entry in row $2$, column $1$?
Which description fits $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$?
options: It has two columns but no rows.

questions.question: When a matrix is used as a coefficient matrix for a linear system, what does it mainly record?
options: The names of the unknowns only.

questions.question: When are two matrices equal?
options: Same size and equal corresponding entries.
When they contain the same set of numbers
When they have the same determinant
When they have the same number of entries

questions.question: If two arrays contain the same four numbers but in different positions, are they necessarily the same matrix?
options: Yes, as long as the sum of entries is the same.
No, the positions of the entries also have to match.
Yes, only the set of entries matters.
No, because matrices cannot contain four entries.
